newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: VNU POSTS HIGHER INTERIM PROFIT DESPITE TV LOSSES.
newsitem.headline: VNU POSTS HIGHER INTERIM PROFIT DESPITE TV LOSSES.

text.p: Dutch publising group VNU reported higher first-half profits on Tuesday despite losses on its commercial television operations.
Net profit from ordinary operations rose 13 percent to 143 million guilders, a slightly higher figure than most analysts had expected, from 126 million in the first half of 1995.
VNU said growth in profits from business information had offset losses on its Dutch and Belgian commercial TV interests.
"With the exception of commercial broadcasting, all groups contributed to the improvement in operating income," it said.
"Most significant was growth at business information in the United States and Europe," it added.
The television business slipped to a loss of six million guilders from a profit of 33 million in the first half of 1995 as increased competition put pressure on advertising rates.
VNU said its RTL4 and VTM channels remained market leader in the Netherlands and Flanders respectively and that it would take tough measures which would lead to better TV results from 1997.

In the Netherlands VNU's RTL4 and RTL5 have had to fight off the challenge of new general interest channel SBS6 and the recently launched specialised channel Sport7 which secured TV rights to all of this season's Dutch league soccer matches.
Consumer magazines, newspapers and educational publishing all made good progress in the first half of 1996, it said.
VNU said it expected growth of profits and earnings per share for the whole of 1996 at least to match the growth rates achieved in the first half of this year.
"In the second half of 1966, results will continue to develop favourably," it said.
However, the company added that it did not expect a marked improvement in market conditions for commercial television in the second half of this year.
